title: toASCII/toUnicode silently drop everything after a second '@'
property: converting an address/domain must not lose characters: an ASCII-only input is returned unchanged
property_test: toASCII/toUnicode preserve text outside the domain in emails with several @
expected: 'a@b@c' (already ASCII, so unchanged; only the domain part is punycoded)
actual: 'a@b' (the '@c' suffix is silently discarded; toUnicode has the same behaviour)
evidence: Docs say 'Only the non-ASCII parts of the domain name will be converted, i.e. it doesn't matter if you call it with a domain that's already in ASCII', and mapDomain says 'Leave the local part (i.e. everything up to `@`) intact'. mapDomain uses domain.split('@') and only keeps parts[0] and parts[1], so parts[2..] are lost. Quoted local parts may legally contain '@' (RFC 5321), so this is data loss rather than a rejected input.
